missions.title: Rooms and hinges: a small Lean proof built from a fixed prior under three error-signal regimes
missions.label: Rooms and hinges
missions.area: Experiment: machine proof search under controlled error signals
missions.rests_on: a licensed Lean statement, one page of a 1964 paper, Mathlib at one commit, and three logged search runs
missions.record_note: Opened 2026-11-25 with the registration of the first build: Erdős Problem 766, the Dirac–Erdős bound. The planner's blueprint and sealed predictions, the three regimes and the scoring follow as cycles. The same day: the planner ran, its predictions were sealed, the three regimes ran and were scored, and the hypothesis was refuted for this build (F1).
record_limits: One theorem, one planner model, one searcher model, one run per regime. The target is 230 to 314 lines of Lean; nothing here speaks to a size where a machine search has been seen to thrash.
The prior held no human argument: the 1964 paper states the result without proof, so the human-experience axis is not measured by this build.
scope_limits: The experiment measures the Lean bridge from a fixed blueprint to a licensed statement; it does not measure mathematical discovery, and it does not check the mathematics of the 1964 argument.
No human-only Lean proof of this statement exists to serve as a control; the existing proof is machine-assisted.

opening.spoken: This record holds an experiment: a small proof is built from a fixed prior, a planner predicts the cost of every step before any search, and the same plan is searched three times with the error signal set differently each time.

short_version.spoken: The shape of a recent machine-built proof of the Riemann hypothesis suggested a search sized to a fast exact error signal, with retries concentrated at the joins. That reading came from one archive with no attempt log. Here the prior is fixed, the plan is drawn once by one model, the cost of each step is predicted and sealed, and a second model searches the plan under full Lean feedback, under accept or reject only, and with no checker until the end. The first target is the Dirac–Erdős bound, Erdős Problem 766, whose Lean statement and only Lean proof both appeared after the searcher model's training cutoff. Result: all three regimes produced the statement as given, the no-checker regime at first try, so the hypothesis as filed is refuted for this build. The signal changed hedging and cost, not success.

what_happened.spoken: On 25 November 2026 the target was chosen from the untracked-claims backlog, the pinned project was built, the registration with eight predictions was committed, and the planner drew sixteen rooms with its cost predictions sealed. Three searchers then filled the rooms in fresh contexts: with full Lean feedback, three calls and done in eight minutes; with one word of feedback, one call per room, sixteen calls, eighteen minutes; with no checker at all, one call at the end, which compiled clean. All three rest on the standard axioms with the statement verbatim. The seal was opened and matched its hash; the control was scored with the same instrument. A fourth arm, asked for by Heidi Bennett after the three: no blueprint, full feedback. The searcher drew its own route in seven lemmas and the file compiled at first check, in three calls and eight minutes.

rely_on.spoken: the three final files compile in the pinned project on the standard axioms with the licensed statement verbatim; the logs and scorer are committed

do_not_rely_on.spoken: any claim that this result carries to larger targets, to a searcher without a blueprint, or to a prior with a human argument; none of those was run

stop.spoken: reading the Alpöge archive's chain-and-retry shape as proof that machine search needs a fast signal to succeed; at this size it did not

new.spoken: hedging rose with the coarseness of the signal (0, 6, 20 first combinators) and so did tokens; the planner over-predicted cost everywhere, most at leaves; the no-blueprint arm and the second target are registered as the next questions; the no-blueprint arm rules out the structure-as-prior explanation at this size, so size is the next variable

certainty_statement.spoken: One finding is refuted under the rule written down first. The next questions are open gaps.

cycles.spoken: Full Lean feedback. The searcher wrote all fifteen nodes and the root before its first call, then made three calls: one error (a decidability instance in the step that moves a graph onto Fin k), one repair, one FINAL that compiled clean on the three standard axioms with the statement verbatim. Eight minutes of a three-hour budget. One helper lemma was added for the floor-arithmetic node; nothing was left unused.

cycles.spoken: One word of feedback, ok or error. The searcher committed one room at a time, sixteen calls in blueprint order and every one ok, then FINAL, clean on the standard axioms. Eighteen minutes and half again the tokens of the full-feedback run. Unable to ask the kernel which spelling of a Mathlib lemma was right, it wrote alternatives into six proofs with the first combinator and let the kernel choose; twelve fallback branches were never executed. It found that the blueprint's route for the floor-arithmetic node does not close as drawn, proved that node directly, and left two nodes proved but unused.

cycles.spoken: No checker until the end. The searcher wrote the whole development blind, from the blueprint and the pinned Mathlib source, and its one allowed call compiled clean on the standard axioms with the statement verbatim. Sixteen and a half minutes and the most tokens of the three. It hedged twenty proofs with the first combinator; twenty-eight fallback branches were never executed, because every primary alternative worked. This is the outcome Heidi Bennett named beforehand as the disproof of the hypothesis as filed.

misses: P3 the planner over-predicted everywhere and missed leaves more than joins

cycles.spoken: Three of eight predictions held. The planner predicted forty-five attempts, half a million tokens and a hundred minutes for the fill; the largest run took sixteen calls, and no node anywhere took more than one. Its misses were over-predictions, larger at leaves than at joins. Against the control, the full-feedback file has twice the declarations at the same depth and shorter steps. The one measure that moved with the signal was hedging: zero, six and twenty first combinators as the signal went from full to one word to none, and tokens rose with it. The hypothesis as filed is refuted for this build.

cycles.spoken: No blueprint, full feedback. The searcher chose its own route, the same vertex-deletion induction the planner had drawn but in seven lemmas instead of fifteen, and the whole file compiled on its first check. Three calls, none an error, eight minutes, fewer tokens than the blueprint run. Three of seven predictions held. The rooms were not what made build 1 cheap; at this size the searcher draws them itself.

findings.spoken: For this theorem, this blueprint and this searcher, the proof did not need the error signal. All three regimes produced the statement as given; the regime with no checker produced it blind, at first try. What changed with the signal was not success but hedging and cost: the searcher wrote more alternatives into its proofs and spent more tokens as the signal got coarser.
